title: Audio Lesson: Session Branching
limitations: Generated from concept pages; not yet reviewed.
Content may drift from source; verify against current main.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Imagine you're 20 messages into a conversation and the agent takes a wrong turn. Without branching, you'd lose everything and start over. Session branching lets you fork from any message and explore an alternative path.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The SessionTree stores conversations as a tree of nodes. The root is your original conversation. When you branch, a new node is created that deep-copies messages up to the fork point. The original stays intact.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Deep copying is essential. If branches shared references, modifying one would corrupt the other. Each branch is fully isolated — you can experiment freely without risk.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The slash-resume command creates a branch at the end of a previous session, effectively continuing where it left off. This is how you pick up work across agent restarts.
